standards.name: ISA Abstract Model
standards.abstract: The ISA Abstract Model is a metadata framework for describing life-science, environmental and biomedical experiments composed of three core entities: Investigation (project context), Study (a unit of research) and Assay (analytical measurements). It is intended to capture experimental metadata including sample characteristics, technology/measurement types and sample-to-data relationships, and is implemented in serializations such as ISA-Tab and ISA-JSON with supporting tools. The specification is maintained by members of the ISA Community (Sansone, Rocca-Serra, Gonzalez-Beltran, Johnson et al.) and addresses the problem of representing complex, multipart experimental investigations so datasets from multiple assay types and workflows can be described, exchanged and integrated.

classification.rationale: The source material presents explicit rows of named properties together with declared datatypes and descriptions (e.g. Investigation, Study, Assay property lists and node property tables). These are concrete field-level metadata definitions (csv-tables) rather than only prose guidance or steps, so the document is best represented as a Metadata Table.

The specification also defines graph constraints (e.g. "Experimental graphs MUST be directed and acyclic" and node-type requirements) and is implemented in ISA-Tab and ISA-JSON serializations; those procedural/graphual elements are documented in the source but the material form is primarily a set of field tables.

standards.name: ISA-Tab format
standards.abstract: ISA-Tab describes a simple, tabular serialization of the ISA (Investigation/Study/Assay) Abstract Model for experimental metadata. It is used to represent investigations that group one or more studies, each study describing subjects/samples and their processing into one or more assays; metadata are recorded in three kinds of tab-separated files (Investigation, Study, Assay) and linked by REF columns. The specification is published and maintained by the ISAtools community (ISA Model and Serialization Specifications) and provides explicit schema/column headings, required section ordering, datatype guidance (strings, dates, ontology term references, files, units) and examples. It addresses the problem of capturing rich, structured experimental metadata in a human- and machine-readable tabular format, with provisions for ontology annotation, file naming conventions and configurable assay templates.

classification.rationale: The source material defines explicit tab-separated files with named column headers and concrete datatypes for those columns (Investigation file sections and Study/Assay column headers). The specification and many example files present genuine field-level structure (column names and types) rather than just prose guidance, so this is a TABLE-style standard.

standards.name: ISA-JSON format
standards.abstract: ISA-JSON is a JSON serialization of the ISA (Investigation/Study/Assay) Abstract Model for describing experimental metadata. It represents investigations containing studies and assays, with materials (sources, samples, extracts), processes, protocols, data files and ontology references. The specification is maintained as part of the ISA Model and Serialization Specifications (ISA team / ISA tools project) and provides JSON Schemas and content rules to ensure ISA-JSON documents validate against the ISA Abstract Model. It addresses the need for a machine-readable, interoperable representation of experimental metadata across multi-assay studies, and covers schemas for Investigation, Study, Assay, Sample, Source, Material, Process, Protocol, Data, Ontology annotations, Person, Publication and related constructs, plus content rules and examples.

classification.rationale: The source material provides explicit JSON Schema definitions for named fields and concrete data types (e.g. "identifier": {"type":"string"}, enums, array/object structures). This is a structured metadata schema (a table of fields with types), not just prose guidance or an ordered workflow.
